subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a TUI observe/mirror mode that can display other channels' sessions, and what opt-in privacy boundary should gate it?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally crosses existing session/channel isolation and may reveal activity from iMessage, Telegram, cron, or sub-agent sessions in a terminal surface; automation cannot choose that security/product boundary.

options.title: Design opt-in observe mode
options.body: Add a read-only TUI observer with explicit operator enablement, identity/session filtering, and tests for same-session and cross-channel privacy boundaries.

options.title: Limit scope to same-session live updates
options.body: Keep this broader request open or close it as not planned after landing the narrower live-update work for already-selected sessions only.

options.title: Use existing diagnostics surfaces
options.body: Document logs, sessions, and Control UI activity as the supported monitoring path instead of adding a cross-channel TUI surface.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in observe mode
recommendation.body: Add a read-only TUI observer with explicit operator enablement, identity/session filtering, and tests for same-session and cross-channel privacy boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the TUI isolation history and merged the current TUI event-handler snapshot, making him the strongest routing candidate for the product/security boundary.
